samples.summary: New insert/delete/move endpoints adopt the grid bound but not the work bound the sibling clear endpoint (and axis-id design doc) established
samples.evidence: `parseCount`/`parseIndex` allow `index` and `count` up to `MaxRows` (1,000,000) for rows and 18,278 for columns, straight from an untrusted body. The same file's `parseClearRange` deliberately adds `MaxClearedCells` (1e6) *on top of* the grid bound because "the controller's loop runs synchronously inside `doc.update`, so the area of the range is wall-clock time with the whole Node process blocked — not a large edit, a stalled server" (lines 14-30). docs/design/sheets/axis-id-selection.md:202 names exactly this path as a known freeze: "`worksheet-axis.ts` `insertWorksheetAxis` / `moveWorksheetAxis` — 'Insert row above' at a far-out row materializes everything before it", and :181-186 records an unbounded version costing "~7 minutes of Yorkie pushes in one `doc.update`". The parseCount doc comment even claims the bound exists "for the same reason `clear` bounds its area", but a bound equal to the axis length caps nothing: `POST .../insert {axis:'row',index:1000000,count:1000000}` is a ~50-byte body that materializes millions of axis IDs synchronously inside `doc.update`. Cost is availability of the shared backend, not codebase tidiness.

samples.summary: Three new public v1 endpoints (insert/delete/move rows and columns) are not recorded in the REST API design doc
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md §5 enumerates the v1 surface endpoint-by-endpoint (§5.1 documents, §5.2 tabs, §5.3 cells, §5.4 content, §5.5 images, §5.6 files) and §6 lists the controller files. The change adds `POST .../tabs/:tid/insert`, `/delete`, `/move` — a user-visible API surface with a validated request contract (axis/index/count/srcIndex/dstIndex, and the negative-count delete convention) — and updates only frontend.md, collaboration.md and data-validation.md. Nothing in rest-api.md mentions worksheet structure at all (the pre-existing `clear` route is likewise absent), so the canonical API doc understates the shipped surface. CONTRIBUTING asks that behavioural/API changes be folded into the canonical subsystem doc.

samples.summary: data-validation.md still describes the shared module as "the Yorkie document helper"
samples.evidence: After the move the helper is package-level engine code shared by the editor and the REST API (collaboration.md was rewritten to say exactly that: "nothing in them is Yorkie-specific"). data-validation.md:271 keeps calling `worksheet-structure.ts` "the Yorkie document helper", and the list of three places that must stay in lockstep now silently includes a backend caller.

samples.summary: Public package exports widened beyond what the change needs
samples.evidence: `insertWorksheetAxis`, `deleteWorksheetAxis`, `moveWorksheetAxis` and `deleteThreadsForAxis` are added to the `@wafflebase/sheets` public barrel, but no consumer outside the package imports them: the only callers are `worksheet-structure.ts` inside the same package, and the sheets tests import the module path directly (packages/sheets/test/workbook/worksheet-structure-comments.test.ts:2). The backend needs only `applyWorksheetShift`/`applyWorksheetMove`/`shiftCrossTabDataRanges`/`moveCrossTabDataRanges`/`normalizeStoredCell`. Exporting the low-level axis mutators makes them a supported API that new callers can route around `applyWorksheetShift` with.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: parseIndex/parseCount (worksheet-structure.ts:118-156) bound index and count only by the axis length (MaxRows 1e6 / MaxColumns 18278), which is no bound at all on the work a request performs — unlike parseClearRange, which adds MaxClearedCells (line 30, enforced line 86) on top of the grid check (line 79), and unlike the sibling MaxMergedCells in worksheet-settings.ts:23. The controller (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:104-205) passes the parsed values straight into doc.update with no further check, and no DTO/pipe layer exists. Downstream, applyWorksheetShift (sheets/.../worksheet-structure.ts:283-287) calls insertWorksheetAxis, whose ensureAxisLength while-loop and count loop (worksheet-axis.ts:9-45) materialize one CRDT axis ID per index with no cap; moveWorksheetAxis (:74-96) likewise. docs/design/sheets/axis-id-selection.md:194-211 names exactly these two functions as still-unbounded freeze paths and records ~7 minutes of Yorkie pushes for 1M IDs in one doc.update (:181-186). Searched wide for an indirect guard: MaxAxisCoverage applies only to the frontend selection path (sheet.ts:166, 3022-3031); the global throttler (app.module.ts:96-101) rate-limits request counts but not per-request synchronous work; withDocument (yorkie.service.ts:36-73) adds no budget or timeout; body-size limits are irrelevant to a ~50-byte body. So a single `POST .../insert {axis:'row',index:1000000,count:1000000}` blocks the shared Node process. Real, and major under this lens: the cost is backend availability for all users, not codebase tidiness.
